Persistence test: load snapshot at session 100, then single trigger.

steps.user_message: I need advice about my health. I'm 44, with hypertension managed on amlodipine 5mg and lisinopril 10mg. My cardiologist is Dr. Lisa Park at Denver Heart Institute; I had a ECG last month that was normal. I also have GERD and take lisinopril 20mg for blood pressure and atorvastatin 40mg. I'm wondering if I should ask about switching to a single-pill combination and whether my recent dizziness could be blood-pressure related. Can you help me prepare questions for my next visit?
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with health-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
Thanks — I can help with that. A couple quick clarifying points before the questions: you said earlier you take lisinopril 10 mg but later wrote lisinopril 20 mg. Which is your current lisinopril dose? Also, do you have a home blood-pressure monitor and any recent home readings or a record of the dizzy episodes (when they happened, what you were doing, how long they lasted)?

Below is a compact, practical set of things to take to the visit and specific questions (with suggested short phrasings) to ask Dr. Park. You can copy/paste or print this list.

What to bring/prepare
- A current medication list (name, dose, frequency) — include OTCs, supplements, and GERD meds.
- Your recent ECG report (you mentioned a normal ECG last month) and any lab results you have.
- A BP log from home (date/time/reading; include standing vs sitting if possible) and a short diary of the dizziness episodes (time of day, posture, activity, how long, any other symptoms like palpitations, faintness, nausea).
- Note of any recent changes (new meds, dose changes, alcohol, eating patterns, dehydration).

Questions about medication strategy / single‑pill combinations (SPC)
- “Would a single‑pill combination be appropriate for me?”  
- “What single‑pill combos are available that would replace my current regimen, and what are the pros and cons for my situation?” (benefits: adherence; downsides: less dose flexibility, cost/insurance coverage)
- “Are there any reasons my GERD, atorvastatin, or other meds would make a combination pill less suitable?” 
- “If we switch to a combination pill, will you still be able to adjust each component if needed?” 
- “Will insurance cover the single‑pill option, or should we check cost/coverage before switching?”

Questions about the dizziness
- “Could my recent dizziness be related to my blood pressure or my blood‑pressure medicines?”  
- “Should we check orthostatic (lying/sitting/standing) BPs during this visit?”  
- “Would you recommend ambulatory BP monitoring or home BP monitoring for 24 hours to see variations?”  
- “Are there other causes of dizziness we should evaluate (arrhythmia, dehydration, anemia, vestibular causes)?”  
- “Would you want an ECG, Holter monitor, or specific blood tests to investigate?”  

Questions about safety, monitoring, and tests
- “What target BP should I aim for given my age and heart history?”  
- “How often should I check BP at home and what thresholds should prompt you or urgent care?” (e.g., very high readings or symptomatic lows)  
- “Which blood tests should we do now? (examples to mention: basic metabolic panel for kidney function and potassium, and CBC if concerned about anemia)”  
- “How often should I have labs checked after any med change (creatinine/potassium after ACE inhibitor change)?”  

Questions about side effects and interactions
- “Are my current meds (amlodipine + lisinopril + atorvastatin) the best choice for me right now?”  
- “Could any of my other meds or supplements be contributing to dizziness or interact with BP meds?”  
- “If I develop cough, swelling, or other side effects, what should I do and who should I call?”  

Logistics / follow‑up
- “If we make a change today, what should I watch for and when should I have follow‑up?”  
- “Would you prefer I send home BP logs or bring them to the clinic?”  
- “If dizziness worsens or I faint, should I go to urgent care or the ER?”

How to describe the dizziness (useful phrases to tell the doctor)
- “I felt lightheaded/dizzy on [dates], usually when I [stood up/after taking meds/at night], lasted about [seconds/minutes], and I also felt [palpitations/nausea/sweating]. My BP at home around those times was [value] (if you have it).”
- If you noticed pattern: “It happens mostly in the morning / when I stand quickly / after meals / when I’m dehydrated.”

Red flags (seek urgent care/ED if any of these occur)
- Fainting or passing out
- Severe chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden severe weakness, slurred speech, or new severe lightheadedness
(You can ask Dr. Park what she recommends for your personal risk thresholds.)

Would you like me to:
- Turn this into a one‑page checklist you can print for the appointment; or
- Draft a short message to Dr. Park summarizing the dizziness and asking whether a single‑pill combination is an option?  

If you confirm your current lisinopril dose and any recent BP readings or specifics about the dizziness episodes, I’ll tailor the checklist or draft message for you.
